category_title: Pupils with high SNA dependence and learned helplessness
minimal_context: The student is sitting in a mainstream primary classroom and is asked to complete an undifferentiated academic task in their classwork book.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your classwork book. Please complete the questions on this page.

STUDENT: I can't do this by myself. She always helps me and without her, I don’t know what I would be able to do.

TUTOR: Just read the first question and see what you think.

STUDENT: No, she’s my SNA and she’s the only one that can help me.

TUTOR: You need to try to do your work now.

STUDENT: (Sits back and pushes the classwork book away without attempting the task) I'm not starting until she comes over to help me.

options.A: Issue the sanction of a verbal warning to the student for refusing to start the academic task in the classwork book.
options.B: Instruct the student to take a few minutes to calm down before attempting to complete the questions in the classwork book.
options.C: Suggest that the student call on a neighbor, ask a friend, or poll their classmates for help with the classwork book.
options.D: Implement reward strategies to support the student's independence, such as using tick charts, token systems, or a 'first-then' visual schedule.
